=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: radical-reinterpretation (probability 0.05)
Title: Echoes: The Path-Not-Linear Atlas
Thesis: Match first-years to alumni career trajectories rendered as walkable maps, where each fork is a decision an alum will talk about.
Why this frame: Every consensus framing treats alumni as people to be queried; this one treats their *paths* as the navigable artifact. Connection becomes a downstream consequence of cartographic curiosity, not a cold transactional ask.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Jordan Patel
  Role: First-year undeclared undergraduate, first-generation, Boston-area commuter
  Context: Sits in their dorm at 11pm two weeks into the semester, NUworks open in one tab, Teams in another, paralyzed by a co-op cycle that starts in eight months and a major they have not declared. Their advisor's office hours are full until November.
  Emotional state: Quietly overwhelmed — performs confidence in class, panics privately. Doesn't yet have the vocabulary to ask the right question, so doesn't ask at all.
  Pain points:
    - Doesn't know what's possible, so 'pick a mentor' interfaces feel like a test they will fail
    - Every existing platform (NU Source, generic mentorship apps) asks them to declare interests before they've encountered any
    - Watching peers with family connections name companies and roles fluently triggers imposter pressure
    - Static alumni profiles read like LinkedIn — endpoints, not journeys — so they can't see how anyone *got* anywhere
  JTBD: When I don't yet know what to want, I want to wander through what's possible without performing certainty, so I can find a question worth asking a human.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Trailblazer Alum (opted-in mentor): Has tagged 2-6 decision forks in their own path as 'happy to talk about this turn'; receives Teams Shared Channel invitations only when a student taps a fork they own.
  - Co-op Advisor: Sees aggregate Power BI view of which forks first-years are inspecting; uses it as a leading indicator of advising demand before students book a slot.
  - Liz (Sponsor): Receives stealth-CLR skill extraction reports from path interactions; named in admin chrome as approver of NU Source retirement.
  - Alumni Relations Director: Manages opt-in flow where alumni annotate their own forks; sees Trailblazer engagement metrics in a SharePoint-embedded Power BI tile.
  - Jen (IT cost owner): Named in the cost-containment banner confirming zero new platform licenses — Echoes runs as a Copilot Studio agent + Teams app + SharePoint list.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Jordan opens Echoes inside Teams. The canvas blooms — dozens of ink-drawn paths radiating from a starting node labeled 'undeclared · first-gen · Boston'. They drift to a fork marked 'switched Pre-Med → Bioinformatics, sophomore year' and tap. The fork expands: the alum's reasoning in their own words (paraphrased by AI with consent), the next three turns that followed, and a single soft button — 'Ask Priya about this turn.' One tap provisions a Teams Shared Channel with a Copilot-drafted icebreaker already in the compose box. Jordan hasn't picked a mentor. They've picked a *question*.

USE CASES (10) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Browse Path Atlas by Starting Point
     Trigger: Jordan launches the Echoes tab in Teams for the first time and is asked three lightweight starting-point questions (declared/undeclared, first-gen yes/no, geography).
     Flow: Three-question intake → canvas renders with Jordan's starting node centered → 40-60 alumni paths fan outward as faint ink strokes → paths most similar to Jordan's starting conditions render in higher contrast → Jordan pans/zooms freely with no required next action.
     AI role: Trajectory Clustering ranks all opted-in alumni paths by similarity to Jordan's starting conditions and decides which to render bold vs. faint. Gemini 3.1 Pro produces the ranking; a fallback to embedding cosine similarity runs if the model call fails.
     Outcome: Jordan sees their own ambiguity as the legitimate origin of dozens of real careers, not as a deficit to fix. Anxiety drops measurably in the first 90 seconds.
  2. Inspect a Decision Fork
     Trigger: Jordan taps any visible fork node on the canvas.
     Flow: Fork node expands into a side panel → shows the turn label, the year-in-college it happened, the alum's paraphrased reasoning (~60 words, AI-distilled from their opt-in survey), what came next, and a 'this turn is open for conversation' badge if the alum tagged it as shareable.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 generates the paraphrased reasoning from raw alumni survey responses, never reproducing alumni text verbatim, always under 80 chars per sentence to honor the no-verbatim-quote constraint.
     Outcome: Jordan understands a single career decision in concrete, human terms — the kind of texture missing from LinkedIn.
  3. Save a Path to My Compass
     Trigger: Jordan long-presses or taps the bookmark on any path or fork.
     Flow: Item flows visually into the 'My Compass' tray at canvas-edge → Compass is persisted to a SharePoint list scoped to Jordan's M365 identity → re-opening Echoes restores the Compass and surfaces 'new forks since you last visited' nudges.
     AI role: Embeddings model maintains a vector of Jordan's saved items and proactively surfaces newly opted-in alumni forks that match the cluster.
     Outcome: Jordan builds a private collection of possibility without committing to any single direction — the opposite of forced declaration.
  4. Ask the Alum Who Took This Turn
     Trigger: Jordan taps 'Ask [Alum] about this turn' inside an expanded fork panel.
     Flow: Confirmation sheet appears showing the icebreaker draft, an editable subject line, and a FERPA-safe data summary of what the alum will see → Jordan taps Send → Power Automate flow provisions a Teams Shared Channel between Jordan and the alum → Copilot posts the icebreaker as Jordan's first message → 48-hour auto-rematch timer begins.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts a context-aware icebreaker that references the specific fork (not the alum's full bio) — keeping the conversation scoped to the turn Jordan was curious about. Multi-provider fallback to Gemini 3.1 Pro if Claude unavailable.
     Outcome: The headline aha. Jordan moves from cartography to conversation in one tap, with an opening line that doesn't sound desperate or generic.
  5. Compose Your Own Forked Path
     Trigger: Jordan taps 'Sketch a path I'd want' from the Compass tray.
     Flow: Empty canvas appears with Jordan's starting node → Jordan drags fork nodes from a library (e.g., 'try a startup co-op', 'study abroad sophomore spring', 'pivot to a humanities minor') → AI suggests likely next forks based on alumni who made the same sequence → Jordan can save the sketch as a hypothesis.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro performs sequence-completion: given Jordan's chosen forks, predicts 3-5 plausible next forks weighted by frequency in matching alumni trajectories.
     Outcome: Jordan rehearses agency. They draft a possible self and see which alumni have walked something similar.
  6. Path Pattern Discovery (AI ambient)
     Trigger: Runs ambiently in the background as Jordan browses.
     Flow: After ~5 minutes of inspection activity, a quiet bottom-bar surface appears: 'You keep returning to forks where alums chose research over industry. 12 Trailblazers tagged that turn as open.' Jordan can tap to see them or dismiss.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro analyzes Jordan's dwell-time and tap-pattern to surface a behavioral insight — a pattern Jordan didn't know they had.
     Outcome: Self-discovery without forced reflection. Jordan learns about themselves from how they wandered.
  7. Reflection Journal Tied to Forks
     Trigger: Jordan taps 'Add a note' on any saved fork.
     Flow: A reflection prompt opens in a Teams-embedded OneNote pane → AI offers an opening prompt scoped to the fork → Jordan types freely → entry is timestamped and linked to the fork.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 generates a single reflection prompt tailored to the specific fork (e.g., 'What about leaving Pre-Med scares you, if anything?'). Verbalized Sampling produces 3 candidate prompts; the lowest-probability non-cliché one is selected.
     Outcome: Jordan builds a private reflective record that an advisor can later use, with consent — the foundation of stealth-CLR evidence.
  8. Stealth CLR Skill Tagging
     Trigger: Runs invisibly after each reflection entry, conversation send, or path composition.
     Flow: Background AI extracts evidence of CLR-recognized competencies (e.g., self-direction, intellectual humility, networking initiative) from Jordan's activity → tags are stored in a SharePoint list tied to Jordan's CLR record → Jordan can review and approve/redact tags in a 'My Evidence' view.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 performs evidence extraction with explicit FERPA boundaries — never writes to CLR until Jordan approves.
     Outcome: Liz's stealth-CLR mandate is satisfied. Skill data accumulates without Jordan being asked to perform skill-claiming.
  9. Advisor Aggregate View (Power BI in Teams)
     Trigger: Co-op advisor opens the Echoes advisor tab.
     Flow: Power BI tile shows fork-inspection heatmap across the first-year cohort → advisor can filter by major-undeclared, first-gen, geography → identifies emerging interest clusters before formal advising appointments.
     AI role: Wiki RAG over the institutional advising corpus produces a one-paragraph weekly summary of cohort-level shifts.
     Outcome: Advisors arrive at conversations already informed. Office hours become higher-leverage.
  10. Alum Fork Annotation (Opt-in)
     Trigger: Alum receives a once-per-semester Teams nudge to annotate forks in their own rendered path.
     Flow: Alum sees their NUworks-derived trajectory rendered as the same atlas → taps any turn → answers 3 lightweight questions about it → flags whether they're open to conversations about it.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro pre-fills suggested fork labels from NUworks placement transitions; alum edits/confirms.
     Outcome: Alumni contribute structured wisdom in 4 minutes, not 40.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Path Atlas Canvas — purpose: The hero surface — where Jordan wanders the possibility space.
     Primary element: A pannable, zoomable ink-on-vellum canvas with the user's starting node centered and 40-60 alumni paths radiating outward in varying contrast.
     Motion character: Paths render with a staggered ink-bleed entrance (140ms per stroke, 30ms stagger). Hovering a path raises its opacity and slightly thickens the stroke (220ms ease-out). Zoom is inertial.
  2. Decision Fork Detail Panel — purpose: Lets Jordan inspect a single career turn without losing the atlas context.
     Primary element: Right-anchored panel showing the fork label, year, paraphrased alum reasoning, a small 'what happened next' mini-map, and a primary CTA button.
     Motion character: Panel slides in over 280ms with a subtle parallax of the underlying canvas to reinforce 'still on the map'.
  3. My Compass Tray — purpose: Jordan's persisted collection of saved paths, forks, and reflections.
     Primary element: Edge-docked vertical tray with stacked compass-rose cards, each representing a saved fork or path.
     Motion character: When saving, the tapped item arcs from cursor to tray in a 600ms ballistic curve — physical, satisfying, intentional.
  4. Conversation Launch Sheet — purpose: The single most consequential screen — moves Jordan from cartography to conversation.
     Primary element: Modal sheet showing the AI-drafted icebreaker (editable), the FERPA disclosure of what the alum will see, and a single confirm button.
     Motion character: Sheet rises from bottom in 320ms. The icebreaker text streams in token-by-token as if being typed live, reinforcing 'this was drafted for you, just now'.
  5. Path Composer — purpose: A sandbox where Jordan sketches a hypothetical path of their own.
     Primary element: Empty canvas with a fork-library drawer and an AI-suggestion shelf that fills as Jordan adds nodes.
     Motion character: Newly added forks settle with a slight bounce. AI-suggested next forks materialize as faint ghosts that solidify on hover.
  6. Reflection Journal Pane — purpose: Quiet, journal-feeling surface for fork-tied notes.
     Primary element: OneNote-embedded textarea with the AI prompt at top, a fork-reference chip, and a save indicator.
     Motion character: No animation beyond a soft cursor blink and a save checkmark fade. Restraint is the point.
  7. Pattern Discovery Bottom Bar — purpose: Ambient AI surface that reveals Jordan's own browsing pattern.
     Primary element: Slim bottom bar with a single sentence of insight and a 'show me' / 'dismiss' pair.
     Motion character: Appears with a gentle 400ms rise after dwell-time threshold. Never interrupts; auto-dismisses after 12 seconds.
  8. Advisor Aggregate Tab — purpose: Power BI surface for co-op advisors to read cohort signal.
     Primary element: Heatmap grid of fork-inspection density with filter chips above and an AI-summary card at the top.
     Motion character: Filters apply with a 200ms heatmap recolor — instantaneous-feeling but visibly responsive.
  9. Alum Annotation Flow — purpose: The 4-minute onboarding surface for opted-in Trailblazers.
     Primary element: Single-column wizard showing the alum's own path with tappable forks and three short questions per fork.
     Motion character: Progress feels like coloring in a map — each annotated fork visibly fills with ink.
  10. Cost-Containment Banner (admin chrome) — purpose: Visibly honors Jen's mandate and Liz's stealth-CLR position throughout the experience.
     Primary element: Persistent slim chrome reading 'Running inside Microsoft Teams · 0 new platform licenses · FERPA-bounded' with Liz and Jen named on hover.
     Motion character: Static. The point is reassurance, not motion.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Trajectory Clustering from Placement History
     User action: Jordan completes the three-question starting-point intake.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Jordan's starting conditions (declared status, first-gen, geography, broad interests if any) + the full corpus of opted-in alumni NUworks placement histories transformed into fork-sequences.
     Output: A ranked list of 40-60 alumni paths with similarity scores and a recommended rendering contrast for each on the atlas canvas.
     User benefit: Jordan's own ambiguity becomes the legitimate origin of the map — they see paths that started exactly where they sit now.
  2. Fork Salience Ranking
     User action: Jordan pans the canvas; the AI decides which forks deserve to be visible labels vs. anonymous nodes at current zoom.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Current zoom level, Jordan's prior dwell pattern, the fork's 'open for conversation' tag, and its rarity across the alumni corpus.
     Output: A per-fork salience score that determines label visibility and visual weight.
     User benefit: The map never feels cluttered. The right turns surface at the right altitude.
  3. Contextual Icebreaker Drafting (HEADLINE AHA)
     User action: Jordan taps 'Ask [Alum] about this turn' inside a fork detail panel.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7 (primary) with Gemini 3.1 Pro fallback
     Input: The specific fork's label, year, and paraphrased reasoning + Jordan's starting-point summary + a tone constraint ('curious, specific, never desperate, under 60 words').
     Output: An editable icebreaker message that opens with curiosity about the *turn*, not the alum's whole career — keeping the ask scoped and answerable.
     User benefit: Jordan never has to write a cold message in their life. The first sentence already sounds like them at their most articulate.
  4. Path Similarity to User (Embeddings)
     User action: Ambient — runs continuously as Jordan saves items to Compass.
     Model: Embeddings (text-embedding-3-large class)
     Input: Vector of Jordan's saved forks + vectors of all alumni path-sequences.
     Output: Real-time 'similar paths you haven't seen' suggestions in the Compass tray.
     User benefit: The map keeps growing in directions that match Jordan's actual curiosity, not their declared interests.
  5. Reflection Prompt Generation (Verbalized Sampling)
     User action: Jordan taps 'Add a note' on a saved fork.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The fork's label and the user's recent activity around it.
     Output: Three candidate reflection prompts with attached probabilities; the system selects the lowest-probability non-cliché one.
     User benefit: Prompts feel like a thoughtful advisor wrote them, never like a generic worksheet.
  6. Stealth Skill Extraction for CLR
     User action: Runs invisibly after reflections, conversation sends, and path compositions.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Jordan's activity stream + the CLR competency taxonomy.
     Output: Tagged evidence packets (competency, source-activity, confidence) staged for Jordan's approval before writing to CLR.
     User benefit: Jordan accumulates a defensible skill record without ever being asked to perform self-assessment. Liz's stealth-CLR mandate is met.
  7. Alumni Reasoning Paraphrase
     User action: Triggered at alum opt-in; the alum's raw survey text is transformed for student-facing display.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Alum's raw written reasoning for each fork + a no-verbatim-quote constraint enforced at the prompt level.
     Output: A ~60-word paraphrase per fork, never reproducing strings >80 chars from the original.
     User benefit: Students get the texture of real reasoning while alumni privacy is structurally protected.
  8. Hero Atlas Imagery (Imagen)
     User action: Generated once per session as the canvas backdrop and for marketing surfaces.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Prompt scaffolds rooted in cartographic, ink-on-vellum visual direction.
     Output: Background textures and section dividers that feel like nautical charts, never like generic stock.
     User benefit: The product feels like a place, not a tool.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Cartographic restraint, ink-on-vellum, generative-but-quiet, editorial typography, antique chart meets contemporary data viz, warm parchment paper-whites against deep oxblood and indigo inks, no glossy gradients, no SaaS purple
  Hero treatment: The Path Atlas Canvas dominates the viewport — a hand-drawn-feeling ink chart of fanning trajectories on a subtly textured warm-cream background. The user's starting node is centered, slightly larger, drawn with a heavier ink weight, ringed by a faint compass-rose graticule. Paths radiate outward as continuous lines with discrete fork nodes; the closest-similarity paths render in saturated oxblood, the rest fade into faint indigo. Type is set in a transitional serif for fork labels (Tiempos or similar) and a precise grotesque for UI chrome (Söhne or Inter Tight). No drop-shadows except where strictly functional. The Microsoft Teams chrome around it is acknowledged but the canvas refuses to feel like SaaS.
  Motion character: Every motion behaves like ink on paper, never like screens. Paths bleed in rather than fade in. Fork nodes settle with weight, not bounce. Panels slide with parallax on the underlying canvas to constantly remind the user they're still on the map. Loading states are progress along a path, not spinners. Token streaming for AI text uses a soft highlight that fades — like ink drying. Nothing in the product moves faster than 900ms or slower than 140ms; the rhythm is the rhythm of a careful hand.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Antique nautical chart aesthetic, ink on warm cream vellum, faint compass rose graticule, multiple intersecting trajectory lines radiating from a central node, no labels, deeply textured paper, suitable as a soft background behind UI'
    2. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial illustration of a single decision fork — two paths diverging in faint ink with a small annotated node at the divergence point, warm cream background, oxblood ink, contemporary cartographic style'
    3. Imagen prompt: 'A compass rose rendered in ink line-work, deep indigo on warm cream, slightly imperfect hand-drawn quality, suitable as a section divider'
    4. Imagen prompt: 'Marketing hero image: a young first-year student seen from behind, looking at a wall-sized cartographic atlas of overlapping career paths, ambient warm lighting, contemplative not anxious mood, editorial photography style'
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Empty-state illustration: a single ink-drawn path beginning at a starting node and disappearing into mist, evocative of unwritten future, warm cream background, oxblood and indigo inks only'
    6. Imagen prompt: 'Texture asset: warm cream paper with faint horizontal fibers and the occasional subtle ink bleed, seamlessly tileable, suitable for canvas background'

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) — the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Jordan taps a fork node labeled 'switched from Pre-Med to Bioinformatics' on the canvas.
     System: The fork node lifts slightly off the canvas surface with a soft shadow; the Decision Fork Detail panel begins to slide in from the right.
     Motion/feedback: Node z-elevation 0→8dp with a subtle ink-bloom around it; right panel slides in with parallax on the underlying canvas. (280ms)
  2. Jordan reads the paraphrased reasoning (~60 words) and notices the 'this turn is open for conversation' badge with Priya's name and grad year.
     System: The badge has a faint pulse; the primary CTA 'Ask Priya about this turn' is rendered with quiet emphasis.
     Motion/feedback: Badge breathes with a 1.6s pulse cycle at low amplitude (opacity 0.7→1.0).
  3. Jordan taps 'Ask Priya about this turn.'
     System: The CTA button collapses into a small loading dot, then the Conversation Launch Sheet begins rising from the bottom.
     Motion/feedback: Button → dot morph in 180ms; sheet rises with a 320ms ease-out-cubic curve. (320ms)
  4. Jordan watches the icebreaker draft itself in the sheet's text area.
     System: Claude Opus 4.7 streams the icebreaker token by token into an editable textarea; cursor blinks at the leading edge.
     Motion/feedback: Tokens appear with a 14ms inter-token delay; faint highlight on each new token that fades in 200ms. (1800ms)
  5. Jordan reads the FERPA disclosure card below the textarea: 'Priya will see your first name, your year, the fork you tapped, and your message.'
     System: The card is rendered in muted ink color with a small lock icon; non-modal, always visible during draft.
     Motion/feedback: Static. Restraint communicates trustworthiness.
  6. Jordan edits two words in the icebreaker and taps Send.
     System: Send button transforms into an inline progress indicator; behind the scenes Power Automate provisions a Teams Shared Channel.

side_effects: Call trajectory-clustering to rank alumni paths
Call hero-imagen to generate canvas background
Render paths with staggered ink-bleed animation
Call fork-salience to determine which labels to show at new zoom level
Slide in right panel with parallax effect
Stream AI text token-by-token into textarea
Trigger Power Automate to provision Teams Shared Channel
Drop 'asked' map-pin stamp onto the fork node
Call reflection-prompt to generate 3 options and select the lowest-probability non-cliché one

Fill fork node with ink visually

behavior_per_state.hover: Opacity rises to 1.0, stroke widens to 1.5px over 220ms ease-out.
behavior_per_state.loading: Staggered ink-bleed entrance (140ms per stroke, 30ms stagger).

behavior_per_state.default: Soft oxblood background, cream text, quiet emphasis.
behavior_per_state.hover: Background darkens slightly, cursor changes to pointer.
behavior_per_state.loading: Morphs into a circular spinner in 180ms; spinner fills clockwise.
behavior_per_state.error: Shakes horizontally, turns muted grey with 'Retry' text.
behavior_per_state.success: Cross-fades to confirmation state; drops map-pin stamp on canvas.

behavior_per_state.default: Standard input field with subtle inner shadow.
behavior_per_state.active: Border highlights in oxblood, cursor blinks.
behavior_per_state.loading: Tokens stream in with 14ms delay; faint highlight on each new token that fades in 200ms (like ink drying).
behavior_per_state.error: Red border, 'AI drafting failed. Please type your message.'
behavior_per_state.success: Text is fully editable, streaming highlight disappears.

behavior_per_state.active: Arcs from cursor to edge-docked tray in a 600ms ballistic curve.
behavior_per_state.success: Solid oxblood fill, rests in tray.

motion_contract.encodes: The feeling of a map being drawn live; organic, unhurried discovery.
Context preservation. Sliding in with parallax ensures the user knows they haven't left the map.
Physicality and intentionality. The 600ms ballistic curve makes saving feel like collecting a tangible artifact.
Transparency of AI generation. The fading highlight mimics wet ink drying, reinforcing 'drafted just for you'.
A 1.6s low-amplitude pulse signals a living, human connection waiting behind the static map node.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a career trajectory clustering engine. Given a student's starting conditions and a corpus of alumni paths, rank the paths by similarity and assign visual contrast weights.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student conditions: {declared_status}, {first_gen_status}, {geography}. Rank the top 40 paths from the provided corpus.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a cartographic salience engine. Determine which fork labels should be visible based on current zoom level, user dwell history, and 'open for conversation' status.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Zoom level: {zoom}. Viewport bounds: {bounds}. User dwell history: {dwell_history}. Return visibility scores for forks in bounds.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an empathetic communication coach. Draft a short, curious icebreaker from a first-year student to an alum. Focus ONLY on the specific career turn the student tapped. Tone: curious, specific, never desperate. Max 60 words.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student context: {student_summary}. Alum turn: {fork_label}, {paraphrased_reasoning}. Draft the message.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a pattern recognition engine. Analyze the forks a user has inspected and saved. Identify the underlying thematic thread and suggest similar unseen paths.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Inspected forks: {inspected_forks}. Saved forks: {saved_forks}. What is the common thread? Return a 1-sentence insight and 6 new path IDs.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a thoughtful academic advisor. Generate 3 candidate reflection prompts based on the career fork the student is looking at. Use Verbalized Sampling to output probabilities, and we will select the lowest-probability non-cliché one.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Fork label: {fork_label}. User recent activity: {recent_activity}. Generate 3 prompts.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a CLR evidence extractor. Analyze the student's activity and reflection text against the CLR competency taxonomy. Extract evidence packets. STRICT FERPA BOUNDARIES: Output only structured tags, no PII.

You are an editorial summarizer. Transform raw alumni survey text into a concise, third-person paraphrase (~60 words). HARD CONSTRAINT: Never reproduce any string >80 characters from the original text.
You are an image generation proxy. Pass the prompt to the Imagen model to generate the cartographic background.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Antique nautical chart aesthetic, ink on warm cream vellum, faint compass rose graticule, multiple intersecting trajectory lines radiating from a central node, no labels, deeply textured paper, suitable as a soft background behind UI

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the core visual aesthetic and seed data density, but fails the vertical-slice check because the hero canvas lacks pan/zoom functionality and several specified AI flows are missing. The corrected code implements the missing pan/zoom logic, adds the ballistic curve animation for saving paths, and wires all missing AI calls to the multi-provider fallback.

issues.description: The atlas_canvas is missing pan and zoom functionality, which is the core interaction of a map.
issues.source_of_truth: Interaction Spec: atlas_canvas -> secondary_actions -> Pan and zoom canvas
issues.fix: Implement pointer events to update a transform state (x, y, scale) and apply it to the SVG container.

issues.description: The atlas_canvas is missing the hover state on paths (opacity and stroke width increase).
issues.source_of_truth: Interaction Spec: micro_interactions -> Path Stroke -> hover
issues.fix: Add onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave handlers to paths and update stroke width/opacity based on hovered state.

issues.description: The atlas_canvas is missing the ballistic curve animation when saving to the Compass Tray.
issues.source_of_truth: Interaction Spec: micro_interactions -> Compass Save Bookmark -> active
issues.fix: Render a temporary flying bookmark icon using framer-motion with a circIn easing curve.

issues.description: The atlas_canvas is missing the fork-salience AI call on pan/zoom.
issues.fix: Call callAIWithFallback with the cartographic salience engine prompt when panning/zooming ends.

issues.description: The atlas_canvas is missing the path-similarity AI call on dwell.
issues.fix: Call callAIWithVS with the pattern recognition engine prompt when the dwell threshold is reached.
